chunks: Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Deliberate cheating (of the gullible) is ill-gotten gain (suh't).

key_terms.الْمُسْتَرْسِلِ: The gullible, the easy-going, or the one who is careless in deals
key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Ill-gotten gain, unlawful sustenance, often obtained by deception or force
key_terms.غَبْنُ: Cheating, defrauding, or exploiting in a transaction

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on cheating the gullible in business transactions?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) equating 'ghabn al-mustarsil'—exploiting the gullible or careless in transactions—with 'suh't', a distinct category of unlawful wealth often associated with deception or unfair advantage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on moral integrity in commerce, warning that taking advantage of another's simplicity constitutes a form of illicit gain that invalidates the spiritual purity of one's earnings.
